children.objective: Use the existing nested pixel loop as a reference and compare materially different work distributions: static assignment by rows, contiguous flattened or collapsed pixel ranges, and a chunked load-balancing schedule. Keep ray generation and intersection logic unchanged to isolate scheduling. Treat threads as a strict maximum, write every pixel exactly once, and report compatible timings at 1, 4, and 40 cores alongside exact-ID, depth-tolerance, and changed-camera/resolution checks.
children.subject: OpenMP pixel-work distribution within the supplied thread budget

children.objective: Use the original per-pixel transform as a reference. Contrast per-call hoisting of invariant camera/raster terms that retains the original per-pixel arithmetic order with row-base plus pixel-increment approaches that may change rounding. First measure variants serially to isolate ray setup; if useful, also measure the best variant combined with T1 to expose interaction rather than treating serial execution as a restriction. Recompute from each call's inputs, assume no fixed camera or resolution, and require exact IDs and the stated depth tolerance on every check. Compare compatible timings, including at one core.
children.subject: Reduce repeated per-pixel ray-generation work

children.objective: Compare localized bounding-box/triangle-kernel improvements with traversal or stack changes, leaving ray generation and pixel scheduling unchanged for attribution. Preserve the original inclusive barycentric and t-range rules and match the final output, including the original equal-distance hit-ID behavior. A changed primitive visitation order is acceptable only if it still reproduces those observable results; do not make same-order traversal a blanket constraint. Avoid scene-specific assumptions and cached hits. Validate exact IDs and depth tolerance across all checks, and compare timings at one core and the official core settings.
children.subject: Optimize scalar BVH traversal and primitive intersection work
